payload.headline: NVIDIA at 155.46 on report day; hold, no swing trade yet

summary.thesis: A grade A business is priced for slower cash-flow growth than it has been delivering. The main risk is that its record 65% operating margin starts to fade.
summary.decision: Hold the long-term position and make no swing trade until the market has reacted to the 2026-11-17 earnings report.

payload.happening: NVDA closed at 155.46, down 0.44% on the day. It is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (192.59), 50-day (211.75) and 200-day (203.6) averages. Earnings are due 2026-11-17, and options price a 9.7% move by 2026-11-20. There has been no news since the last note.
payload.business: The business numbers are strong. Latest-quarter sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%, and trailing free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 127.0B from 72.0B. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 23.2B. Three things are at risk. First, the margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%). Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. Third, the newest filed quarter ended 2026-07-26, so today's report is not yet in this data. Insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. That is a governance and sentiment signal, not a change to demand or cash. The weak tape and the elevated fear in tech (macro view) also affect sentiment rather than the business. Segment detail is not available.

worth.text: At 155.46, the cash-flow model implies that free cash flow starts growing about 20.9% a year and then slows. That is well below the 83% sales growth of the last year. The model gives 150.22 at 20% starting growth and 218.73 at 30%. The DCF (a model that values the future cash flows) gives 189.87 in the bear case, 220.46 in the base case and 261.33 in the bull case. The company's own past price-to-sales ratios point to 217.35–411.04. The stock trades at 19.6 times trailing earnings and 9.8 times next year's estimated earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio of 12.4 is below the peer median of 15.7 and sits at the 4.0 percentile of its own 5-year history. The gap between methods comes down to one thing: how long the current growth and margin last. If operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 112.91. At 32%, it drops to 75.59.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%.

bull: Sales growth sped up to 105.85% a year in the latest quarter, from 73.21% two quarters ago.
Free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B, and net cash is 23.2B.
The stock trades at 9.8 times next year's estimated EPS of 15.84, and its price-to-sales ratio of 12.4 is below the peer median of 15.7.
bear: Operating margin of 65.21% is at the top of its 5-year range. At 48%, the model value falls to 112.91.
Unpaid customer bills grew 127% against 106% sales growth, which suggests sales may have been pulled forward.
The trend is down: the price is below the 50-day average of 211.75, and insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Today's close. It implies 20.9% starting cash-flow growth, which is enough to keep holding but leaves too little proof to add before the report.
The value at 20% starting growth, just above the 147.59–150.01 support zone. Add here if the report shows operating margin near 65.21% and customer bills growing in line with sales.
The value at 30% starting growth, close to the DCF base of 220.46. Trim here, because most of the modelled upside would be used up.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the business is grade A, but the committee call is 'Hold' and the macro, technical and risk views are negative. The value supports holding. The customer-bill warning and the unreleased quarter argue against adding yet.

swing.why: Options imply 103.6 volatility against 53.8 realized, a ratio of 1.92, so the report could gap the price through a stop under 147.59. The first resistance at 163.9–169.14 also leaves little room on the upside.

decision.timing: No trade until the market has reacted to the 2026-11-17 report. Then compare revenue with the 108.7B estimate, EPS with 2.47 and next-quarter guidance with 124.9B before acting at 150.22 or 218.73.

change_mind: If the report shows operating margin falling toward 48%, the value drops to 112.91. The action would move from hold to trim.
A close below the 147.59–150.01 support zone would turn the add level into a wait. A close above 175.15 would end the run of lower highs and support adding.
If next-year EPS estimates fall from 15.84 toward the low of 11.85, the 9.8 forward P/E would no longer be cheap, and the action would move to wait.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold long-term and no swing trade. There is no news since the last note and the report's figures are not in DATA yet, so the close of 155.46 still implies only 20.9% starting growth.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
